t.E626.agn: JECFA set a group ADI 'not specified' for guanylic acid and its calcium, disodium and dipotassium salts (last evaluation 1993) and stated that intake from additive use is far below that of natural nucleotides from foods. In JECFA's 1974 evaluation it was reported that intake of large amounts of these compounds in humans may increase blood uric acid levels and urinary uric acid excretion, and that this should be taken into account for people predisposed to gout and for those taking diuretic medicines that reduce uric acid excretion.
t.E626.body: Guanylates occur naturally in all animal and plant tissues; in the body they are broken down to uric acid via guanosine, guanine and xanthine.
t.E626.eff.0.t: May increase blood uric acid levels and urinary uric acid excretion
t.E626.eff.0.w: People predisposed to gout and those taking diuretic medicines that reduce uric acid excretion
t.E626.eval: A flavour enhancer that strengthens umami (savoury, meaty) taste. JECFA set a group ADI 'not specified' for guanylic acid and its calcium, disodium and dipotassium salts (last evaluation 1993); intake from additive use is far below that of natural nucleotides from foods. It is broken down to uric acid in the body; in 1974 JECFA stated that large amounts should be taken into account for people predisposed to gout. EFSA's re-evaluation is ongoing.
t.E626.prod: Produced by microbial fermentation or by breaking down RNA obtained from yeast.
t.E626.regx.0: ADI not specified (group ADI for guanylic acid and its salts).
t.E626.regx.1: In the E 626–635 ribonucleotides group; authorised at quantum satis in salt substitutes and seasonings/spice blends.
t.E626.regx.2: Re-evaluation ongoing; a call for data was published in 2023 (deadline 31.03.2024).
t.E626.summary: Guanylic acid and its salts: flavour enhancers from the nucleotide group. Usually used together with glutamate in instant soups and seasonings.
t.E626.what: A flavour enhancer that strengthens meaty (umami) taste in food; a derivative of guanosine 5'-monophosphate (GMP).
